I baked brownies last night to bring in for Halloween. I used **MIGHTYLICIOUS brownie mix**, **Hu Kitchen chocolate chips**, **Melt Organic plant-based butter**, vegan yogurt, water, and a little organic vanilla extract. I wanted something I could share without using eggs or dairy in the recipe, and the extra chocolate chips seemed like a good idea.

The decorating part didn't quite go to plan. I'd ordered organic vanilla frosting and candy eyes to make little Halloween faces, but the grocery delivery showed up late, and the frosting was replaced with **Pillsbury Creamy Supreme Vanilla**. By then I was on my way, so I packed the brownies into paper muffin liners and brought the decorations along.

I'm leaving some plain and adding frosting and **Betty Crocker candy eyes** to the others. Nothing elaborate—just a bit of Halloween fun.

**A note for anyone with food allergies:** The chocolate chips and plant butter contain coconut. Hu's chips have a shared-equipment warning for milk and peanuts. The frosting and candy eyes contain soy, and the candy eyes use confectioner's glaze, so I wouldn't call the decorated ones vegan. The plain brownies were made with plant-based ingredients, but not in an allergen-free kitchen. If you have a serious allergy, please check the packaging before trying one.

Happy Halloween!
